title: Seaborn Analytics — integration scratch diary
body:
Context / quick summary:
- Intro call 2025-10-31 w/ Seaborn Analytics (lead: Claire Torres, infra: Mateo Ruiz). Seaborn builds patient-outcome dashboards for regional clinics — strict PHI rules in EU + US. Want LLM for note summarization + anomaly detection triage.
- They asked about: private deployment options (VPC + on-prem hybrid), KMS integration, retention/audit, and expected per-request latency. Also curious about Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for their workload.

Key constraints they emphasized:
- Data residency: EU-first. Some hospitals cannot send any PHI outside EEA. Must support customer-managed key (HSM/KMS) and can be air-gapped for a subset of nodes.
- Latency: median 120–200ms desired on single-utterance summarization (average 600 tokens input, 200 tokens output). They accept slightly higher p95 if throughput preserved for batching.
- Throughput: peak 120 reqs/min for batch jobs during morning ingestion window; sustained low traffic otherwise.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budgets — prefer predictable reserved pricing; will consider Dedicated if we can guarantee capacity for morning window and private control.
- Compliance: need HIPAA + SOC2 readiness audit artifacts; full audit logs on model inputs/outputs retention configurable.

Observed gotchas / red flags from the call:
- They currently ETL notes into a compressed JSONL store; client-side prose has noisy tokens (lots of templates + OCR artifacts). Prompt engineering must include cleaning step — otherwise hallucinations.
- Some clinics use older encoding (Windows-1252) in EHR exports — connector must normalize UTF-8.
- They asked whether Redwood supports selective KV caching for specific clients (i.e., do not persist across sessions for sensitive patients). We do, but need to document config knobs for per-customer cache TTLs and eviction.
- Concerned about cross-tenant leakage with shared caches on Hosted. We should call out default isolation differences between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Initial technical notes (ideas + ops):
- Recommend Private (VPC) deployment in eu-west-1 for EU residency + HSM. Option: Private control plane + customer-managed HSM for keys. Note: on-prem will be heavier — ask for sizing of GPU hosts.
- For latency: use a low-latency variant/model (quantized LLM with Redwood optimized kernels) + smaller response model for summarization (200 token output). Benchmark locally with 600-in/200-out profile.
- Batching strategy: plan for mixed-mode — immediate small inference (interactive) + scheduled bulk summarization. Suggest two pools: interactive dedicated (lower batch sizes, pinned capacity) and bulk workers (higher batch sizes, preemptible).
- KV/Prefix caching: include client-scoped prefix caching for longitudinal patient notes to improve throughput on follow-ups. Provide opt-out toggle per patient ID.
- Retention & audit: default to 30d logs for dev; enterprise policy up to customer-defined retention. For HIPAA they want 7 years of audit trails — we have to confirm storage tier/cost impact.
- Network: need static IPs for clinic allow-lists. For Private, ensure NAT + egress policies documented.

Experiment plan (minimum viable test):
1) Proof-of-concept: simple summarization pipeline deployed to a Private staging VPC in eu-west-1. Use 1x mGPU instance (TBD) with quantized-medium model. Objective: p50 < 200ms for 600-token inputs.
2) Data hygiene: provide a connector script to normalize encodings, strip known OCR artifacts, and a tiny heuristics step to remove template headers. Run on 1k sample notes.
3) Quality eval: generate 1k summaries, run rouge/semantic-sim tests + clinical reviewer spot-check (Claire will coordinate 3 clinicians).
4) Cost & capacity: simulate morning window (120 reqs/min) and validate autoscale / reserved capacity plan.

Open questions to resolve with Seaborn:
- Exact GPU SKU preference/cost sensitivity: do they want to own reserved capacity or buy a committed Dedicated pool? (Action: ask Mateo for target MRR budget range)
- Do they require FIPS endpoints for KMS/HSM? (Action: Claire to check with their infosec)
- Will they accept aggregated telemetry or need token-level logs for every inference? (privacy tradeoff)
- Do they have any pre-existing certs for our on-prem installer (e.g., approved sysadmins, SIEM integration)?

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Maya: send follow-up email with 1-page architecture sketch + ask for sample notes (anonymized) — due 2026-03-12.
- Ravi: rough cost estimate for 2 deployment options (Dedicated reserved vs Private VPC w/ HSM) — due 2026-03-18.
- Anya: draft quick connector script (encoding normalizer + OCR cleanup heuristics) + sample CLI usage — due 2026-03-14.
- Claire (Seaborn): confirm compliance checklist items and whether they can provide a sanitized sample dataset — target 2026-03-15.

Notes-to-self / talking points for next call:
- Emphasize isolation differences: hosted (shared infra, faster time-to-value) vs dedicated (reserved capacity + isolation) vs private (customer VPC + control plane, best for PHI).
- Be transparent about p95 tradeoffs when using batching — offer canary approach: small pool for interactive, larger pool for batch.
- Offer to run a 2-week trial in private staging with access logs and cost telemetry visible.

Quick checklist before demo:
- [ ] Confirm sample notes received (Claire).
- [ ] Provision eu-west-1 staging VPC (infra request ID?).
- [ ] Prototype connector + small dataset run (Anya).
- [ ] Baseline latency run (Maya + infra).

Random snippets I want to include in the follow-up email:
- "We can meet the EU residency requirement via Private (VPC) deployments with customer-managed KMS; for highest assurance we offer an on-prem air-gapped option for the ingestion pipeline."
- "Two recommended patterns: 1) interactive pool (low-latency, reserved) for clinician-facing queries; 2) batch pool (high-throughput, cost-optimized) for nightly processing."

End-of-diary entry.

(If this grows beyond a day — move to a shared drive draft in /shared_drives/solutions-engineering/ to hand off formally.)
